Engineering Leadership Skills Repo

Engineering leadership is pattern work. I'm treating it that way.

Lee OveryAug 21, 2026

Every promotion into leadership arrives with the same lie attached: that the job is the same job with more people in it. It is not. The work stops being the thing you make and becomes the conditions under which other people make things, and almost nothing you learned as a senior engineer transfers without translation.

What does transfer is the habit of looking for patterns. A recurring argument between two teams is a boundary drawn in the wrong place. A review queue that never drains is a staffing decision nobody made out loud. A launch that slips twice for unrelated reasons is usually one related reason wearing two costumes. Reading those as patterns rather than as incidents is the whole discipline, and it is learnable the way refactoring is learnable: by collecting cases until the shapes become obvious.

So I am keeping a repository of them, one file per pattern: the situation that produces it, the tells that identify it early, and what actually worked. Not advice — cases. Advice generalizes too fast and loses the conditions it depended on, and the conditions are the part that decides whether the move works for you.
